title: Applied ML Evals: Integrated Onboarding, Prompt Sets, Quantization, and Regression Triage Playbook
author: Aisha Thompson
content:
Summary:
This playbook defines Redwood's integrated process for onboarding models into the eval-harness, building and curating prompt sets and benchmarks, producing quantization profiles, and performing regression triage. It consolidates standards and operational steps so model owners, applied ML engineers, and SREs can onboard models quickly while keeping quality and cost guardrails enforced.

Scope:
- Applies to any model being served on Redwood (hosted, dedicated, private) that will be included in our eval harness or shipped to customers.
- Covers: eval-harness onboarding, prompt-set standards, benchmark construction, quantization profiling, automated regression detection, and manual triage/runbook.

Goals and measurable SLOs:
- Time-to-onboard: 5 business days from intake to a first-pass evaluation in the harness.
- Coverage: Each model must have at least 3 domain prompt-sets and 2 general-purpose prompt-sets before production rollout.
- Regression detection sensitivity: >90% recall for regressions that degrade reference prompts' pass-rate by >=5 percentage points.
- Regressions triage SLA: High-severity regression acknowledged within 1 hour and mitigated or rolled back within 8 hours.

Ownership and roles:
- Model Owner: primary contact for the model (responsible for artifacts, model card, and remediation).
- Applied ML (Evals) Team: owner of eval harness, prompt-set repository, and regression-monitoring rules.
- Quantization Team: owns quantization profile generation, validation harness, and acceptable tolerance thresholds.
- SRE/Platform: deploy/run infrastructure, alerts, and rollback tooling.
- Customer Success: escalation point for customer-impacting regressions.

Onboarding checklist (step-by-step):
1. Intake & triage (Model Owner)
   - Submit model onboarding form (link: /onboarding/form).
   - Provide model card: architecture, checkpoint hash, training data summary, recommended seq lengths, and intended use-cases.
2. Artifact staging (Model Owner)
   - Push model artifacts to staging bucket: s3://redwood-staging/models/<model-id>/<version>/
   - Provide compatibility shim or config (example: runtime-config.yaml).
3. Baseline eval (Applied ML)
   - Run eval-harness baseline suite (command):
     ```bash
     eval-harness run --model s3://redwood-staging/models/<model-id>/<version> --suite baseline --out results/<model-id>-baseline.json
     ```
   - Capture baseline metrics: pass-rate, BLEU/ROUGE (if applicable), perplexity, mean latency p50/p95, cost-per-1k-tokens.
4. Prompt-set and benchmark assignment (Applied ML)
   - Assign the model to the recommended prompt-sets by capability tag (see Prompt-set standards).
5. Quantization profiling (Quantization Team)
   - Generate 8-bit/4-bit candidate profiles with the profiling harness.
   - Validate candidate quantized models with held-out prompt-sets (see Quantization validation thresholds).
6. Rollout gating (Applied ML + Platform)
   - Gated rollout only if no high-severity regressions and metrics within tolerances.
   - Document rollout policy: canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 48 hours with automated rollback on metric regression.

Prompt-set standards:
- Naming: <domain>-<capability>-v<major> (e.g., customer-support-summary-v1).
- Metadata per prompt-set (example JSON in appendix): must include domain, expected output type, pass/fail criteria, and edge-case tags.
- Size & diversity: 100–1,000 prompts per major prompt-set; include: canonical examples (20%), adversarial examples (20%), edge cases (20%), long-context cases (20%), and paraphrase variants (20%).
- Benchmarks: maintain a gold/reference answer for deterministic scoring when applicable; where free-text, define evaluation rubric (semantic equivalence, factuality, safety).
- Versioning: any change to a prompt-set must increment major version and be accompanied by a rationale and diff.

Quality guardrails and thresholds:
- Automatic guardrail checks during onboarding and CI:
  - Pass-rate: >= 85% on general-purpose prompt-sets (>= 90% recommended for production).
  - Latency: p95 <= 1.5x baseline p95 for comparable model class.
  - Cost: estimated token cost delta <= +25% vs baseline unless compensated by >5% quality gain.
  - Safety: zero critical safety violations on curated safety prompt-sets.
- Tolerance windows for quantized variants:
  - 8-bit: quality delta <= 3 percentage points on pass-rate across core prompt-sets.
  - 4-bit: quality delta <= 7 percentage points (requires explicit sign-off).

Quantization profiling and validation:
- Profiling process:
  1. Run calibration dataset through profiling harness to collect activation distributions.
  2. Generate candidate quantization profiles (.qprof) for per-layer symmetric/asymmetric schemes.
  3. Evaluate candidate profiles against the quantization validation suite.
- Validation metrics to capture: pass-rate delta by prompt-set, token-level accuracy where applicable, perplexity change, and per-request latency & memory.
- Example quantization pipeline commands:
  ```bash
  qprof generate --model s3://... --calib-data s3://... --out /tmp/<model>-qprof
  qprof validate --model s3://... --qprof /tmp/<model>-qprof --suite quant-val --out /tmp/quant-results.json
  ```
- Accept/Reject criteria: a profile is accepted for production if it meets the tolerance windows in Quality guardrails and does not introduce any new safety violations.

Automated regression detection:
- Signals monitored: prompt-set pass-rates, percentiles of latency, model-output similarity drift (embedding-based), and safety-violation counts.
- Alert thresholds (examples):
  - Alert Level: warning -> pass-rate drop >= 3 percentage points on any core prompt-set sustained for >= 30 minutes.
  - Alert Level: critical -> pass-rate drop >= 5 percentage points OR safety violation >=1 on production prompt-set.
- Alert routing: PagerDuty -> Model Owner & Applied ML on-call -> SRE on-call.

Regression triage workflow (high-level):
1. Acknowledge (within 1 hour for critical) and collect initial telemetry (correlation id, request sample, model version, recent deployments).
2. Reproduce locally using the eval-harness with the failing prompt-set and a snapshot of production request logs.
3. Determine scope: single prompt-set, model-wide, or infra-induced (latency/OOM).
4. If model-only regression: revert to previous model or deploy a compatible fallback.
5. If infra-induced: engage SRE to mitigate and stabilize.
6. Root-cause analysis and postmortem within 5 business days for critical regressions.

Runbook: triage a high-severity regression (step-by-step):
1. PagerDuty alert fires -> on-call acknowledges and posts to #eval-regression channel.
2. Triage lead (Applied ML) runs:
   ```bash
   eval-harness run --model-version <version> --prompt-set <failing-set> --replay-logs s3://redwood-prod-logs/recent/ --out /tmp/repro.json
   ```
3. Compare outputs with baseline: diff-outputs.py /tmp/repro.json results/<baseline>.json --metrics pass-rate, embedding-similarity
4. If outputs show degradation >=5pp on core sets -> mark P0 and trigger rollback plan.
5. Rollback plan (Platform): rollback to model version <previous-version> using deployment service:
   ```bash
   deployctl rollback --service model-serving --model-id <model-id> --target-version <previous-version>
   ```
6. Validate rollback success by re-running the failing prompt-set.

Post-incident analysis and actions:
- Required artifacts: reproduction case, root cause hypothesis, timeline of events, commit(s) implicated, remediation steps, and follow-ups.
- Typical remediation actions: update prompt-sets (if brittle), adjust quantization profile, improve runtime kernels, or strengthen pre-deploy checks.
- Add regression to the central triage board and tag with: severity, root-cause-category, and estimated effort.

Operational tooling and dashboards:
- Dashboards: per-model SLO dashboard (pass-rate by prompt-set, latency distribution, cost-per-1k-tokens).
- Alerts: configured in PagerDuty with automated runbook links.
- Repro tooling: repro-helper CLI and eval-harness that can replay traffic and run diffing tools.

Appendix A: Example prompt-set metadata (JSON snippet)
```json
{
  "name": "customer-support-summary-v1",
  "domain": "customer-support",
  "expected_output_type": "extractive_summary",
  "pass_criteria": "F1 >= 0.75 OR human-judgement >= 4/5",
  "size": 250,
  "edge_case_tags": ["long-context", "sarcasm", "code-snippet"]
}
```

Appendix B: Typical metric table (for gating)
| Metric | Gate threshold | Production target | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Prompt-set pass-rate (general) | >= 85% | >= 90% | Measured on baseline prompt-sets |
| Latency p95 | <= 1.5x baseline | <= 1.2x baseline | Compare model-class peers |
| Safety violations | 0 | 0 | Any critical safety violation fails gate |
| Token-cost delta | <= +25% | <= +10% | Cost vs baseline model |
